lines.text: In eighteen fifty-nine, America and Britain almost went to war... over a pig.
San Juan Island sat right between them, and both countries said it was theirs.
Then, on June fifteenth, a farmer named Lyman Cutlar found a pig eating his potatoes.
Problem: the pig belonged to the British Hudson's Bay Company.
The British threatened to arrest him. So the Americans called the army.
Captain George Pickett landed with sixty-four soldiers.
By the end of August, four hundred sixty-one Americans and fourteen cannons faced five British warships and over two thousand men.
Then a British admiral said no. He would not start a war between two great nations over a squabble about a pig.
For twelve years, two armies shared one island. Their officers even met up for whisky and cigars.
In eighteen seventy-two, the German Kaiser finally settled it. The island went to America.
The total number of casualties in the whole war? One pig.
